# Sirach Chapter 32 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 32 | **Agents Consulted:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA

---

## Council Notes

Chapter 32 addresses three settings: the banquet (vv. 1–13), the seeking of divine guidance (vv. 14–17), and practical prudence (vv. 18–24). The "master of the feast" (symposiarch) was a recognized social role in Hellenistic culture. Verse 5's musical simile should preserve the jewelry imagery. The closing verses shift to general wisdom about obedience and trust; v. 24 ends the chapter on a note of assurance.

---

**32:1** Have they appointed you master of the feast? Do not exalt yourself; be among them as one of them. Take care of them and then take your seat.

**32:2** And when you have fulfilled all your duties, recline, so that you may be glad on their account and receive a garland for your good conduct.

**32:3** Speak, elder, for it is fitting for you, but with sound judgment, and do not interrupt the music.

**32:4** Where there is entertainment, do not pour out speech; display not your wisdom out of season.

**32:5** Like a ruby seal on a setting of gold is a concert of music at a wine feast.

**32:6** Like an emerald seal set in a gold mounting is the melody of music with fine wine.

**32:7** Speak, young man, only if you must — yet scarcely, and only when asked more than once.

**32:8** Be concise; say much in few words. Be as one who knows, and yet also knows how to hold his tongue.

**32:9** Among persons of rank do not act as their equal, and when another is speaking, do not chatter on.

**32:10** Lightning flashes before thunder, and before a man of genuine character, grace goes before him.

**32:11** Rise at the right time and do not be the last; go home promptly and do not linger.

**32:12** There enjoy yourself and do what your heart desires, but do not sin through proud speech.

**32:13** For all these things bless your Maker, who fills you with his good things.

**32:14** Whoever fears the Lord will accept his correction, and those who seek him early will find his favor.

**32:15** Whoever seeks the law will be filled by it, but the hypocrite will stumble over it.

**32:16** Those who fear the Lord will find true judgment, and they will kindle righteous deeds like a light.

**32:17** The sinful person shuns reproof and finds a rationalization according to his own will.

**32:18** A sensible person will not disregard a misgiving, and a proud and reckless person will not shrink back when caution is needed.

**32:19** Do nothing without deliberation, and when you have acted, do not be plagued by regret.

**32:20** Do not travel a way full of obstacles, and do not stumble on stony ground.

**32:21** Do not put confidence in a road with no apparent hazards, and beware of your own inclinations.

**32:22** In all your actions guard yourself, for this too is the keeping of the commandments.

**32:23** Whoever keeps the law keeps himself, and whoever trusts in the Lord will suffer no loss.

**32:24** No evil will befall the one who fears the Lord, but in trial he will be rescued again and again.
